Seems like you've gone a while without a reply so I'll just spitballs something. I remember hearing that some substances can be harmful to the lifetime of the vape device itself. Somethings get gunked up on the heating element and somethings start to eat at the tank. There probally doesn't seem to be too much demand for those flavors.

The limitations (afaik) for flavoring agents are:
They need to be soluble and mix with the compound. & They need to not reduce the lifespan of the vape device

((Disclaimer: Just a geek passing through, not a fan of vape and/or smokeing))

Look for ginger flavors. They're hard to find and pretty hit and miss, but before they stopped selling it, mtbakervapor used to have the most delicious, spicy straight-up ginger flavor. You might have some luck if you look hard enough.

Also, capsaicin, the compound that gives chilies and peppers their 'heat', is a pretty potent irritant. That's why they use it in pepper spray. So, you don't want to aerosolize it into your lungs.

I think the closest thing to spicy that you are going to find readily available in most places is some type of cinnamon flavor. I've tasted some that have quite a kick to them, especially at a higher nic level.

I like coffee and nut flavors for non-sweet vaping. Though some of them also come in extremely sweetened variants. You'll have to try your luck.

I have not (yet) tried any salty flavors. Mostly because people who have tried them reported that they tasted like soup powder and taste and smell stay in your tank forever. Still have some flavorings lying around here waiting for me to have more courage.

If you were to, FlavourArt has tobacco flavorings like Shade, Perique, and Burley tobacco that all have spikes of that peppery smack. I love the stuff, myself, and vape them quite often. At the very least, check out that Coval juice - it is Perique, nail-on-the-head, I guarantee it. It'll scratch that itch you've got for something at the complete, polar opposite side of the spectrum from creamy desserts. But, again, I think you might really take to mixing your own stuff.
